name: Doha Bank
founded: 1978/1979 (incorporated 15 March 1979 under Emiri Decree No. 51 of 1978; first branch opened 1979; QSE-listed 1997)
ownership_summary: QSE-listed with 3,187 shareholders at 31 Dec 2025. The Articles cap any holder at 5%, except the State of Qatar, Qatar Foundation, GRSIA pension funds, QIA and Qatar Holding. At 31 Dec 2025 QIA held 5% directly and indirectly and the General Retirement and Social Insurance Authority pension funds held 6.47% (Governance Report 2025). The Q2 2026 investor presentation gives State of Qatar ownership of 11.47% at 30 Jun 2026.

shareholders.holder: General Retirement and Social Insurance Authority (pension funds)

government_link: Yes - State of Qatar ownership 11.47% at 30 Jun 2026 (S7), made up of GRSIA pension funds 6.47% and QIA 5% at 31 Dec 2025 (S6). QIA and GRSIA each have a board representative (S2).
group_structure: Doha Bank (Q.P.S.C.) is the QSE-listed parent with overseas branches in the UAE, Kuwait and India (2) and representative offices in Bangladesh, China, Japan, Singapore, South Africa, Turkey and the UK (Nepal is also listed at FY2025). Principal subsidiaries (30 Jun 2026): Sharq Insurance L.L.C. (100%, QFC general insurance, formerly Doha Bank Assurance), Doha Finance Limited (Cayman, debt issuance) and DB Securities Limited (Cayman, derivatives). Associate: Doha Brokerage and Financial Services Limited (India, 35.29% at FY2025, brokerage and asset management). There is no Qatar brokerage or asset management subsidiary: QSE trading runs through partner The Group Securities (Q-Trade). Doha Bank founded the QE Index ETF (QETF), which is managed by Aventicum Capital Management (Qatar).

subsidiaries.name: Sharq Insurance L.L.C.
subsidiaries.activity: General insurance (QFCRA-licensed); est. 2007 as Doha Bank Assurance

footprint: Qatar at 30 Jun 2026: 13 domestic branches, 1 corporate branch with a linked corporate service centre, 3 e-branches, 70 ATMs and 3 ITMs (20 domestic branches at end-2023). Overseas: branches in the UAE (Dubai), Kuwait and India (Mumbai, Kochi), plus representative offices in 7 countries (S3 note 1, S7 p.7).
customer_segments: Retail: Qatari nationals and expatriates (about 62% of the retail asset book is Qatari), with payroll/WPS, upper-mass and affluent focus (Al Dana prize savings, Riyada). Private Banking: HNW and UHNW clients. Wholesale: corporates, SMEs, public sector, financial institutions (400+ FI relationships). About 300,000 active customers at 30 Jun 2026 (salaried, non-salaried and WPS).
business_lines: Business groups: Wholesale Banking, Treasury & Investments, International Banking, Retail Banking, and Private Banking & Wealth Management (AR 2025). Private Banking gives clients an investment account on the Bank of Singapore platform (global equities, funds, fixed income, structured products, FX, Lombard) and offers wealth planning (estate, trusts, family governance, philanthropy). The Wealth Management Division, a recent creation, added Shariah-compliant products and a Swiss global custody account with UBS; AUM was above USD 100m in 2025. Private markets are offered through Blackstone (partnership Q2 2025), with MoUs with Carlyle (2024) and KKR (Sep 2026). Investment and trading channels: DB Global Markets (DBGM) platform for US and European stocks, bonds, FX and metals; International Brokerage (US, Canada, UK and Europe shares, ETFs and options; from USD 5,000); Q-Trade for QSE trading through The Group Securities; margin trading. Bancassurance (MetLife investment-linked plans) and Sharq Insurance.

capabilities.wealth_summary: Private Banking & Wealth Management is one of Doha Bank's five business groups and is led by Chief Private Banking & Wealth Management Officer Antonio Genovese. Doha Private Banking (HNW/UHNW; no published threshold) gives clients a dedicated banker and an investment account on the Bank of Singapore platform. That account covers global equities, funds, fixed income, structured products, FX, Lombard lending, estate planning and life insurance, with Bank of Singapore research and risk profiling. Product menus also list hedge funds and private-market funds, private equity, trusts and family governance. A Wealth Management Division created recently launched a Swiss global custody account with UBS and Shariah-compliant products in 2025; division AUM topped USD 100m. Private markets come through Blackstone (strategic partnership formed Q2 2025), plus MoUs with Carlyle (Oct 2024) and KKR (Sep 2026). Self-directed investing runs through the DB Global Markets platform (US and European stocks, bonds, FX and metals; revenue QAR 3.2m in 2025), International Brokerage, and Q-Trade, which reaches QSE through partner The Group Securities from online and mobile banking. Awards: MEED Best Private Equity Offering MENA 2025; Euromoney Private Banking Awards 2026 Qatar Best for Client Service and Best for Funds.

private_banking.detail: Doha Private Banking gives each client a dedicated private banker, preferential pricing, and an investment account on the Bank of Singapore platform, with Bank of Singapore research and risk profiling. Services cover asset creation and preservation, wealth planning (estate planning, family governance, philanthropy advisory, trust services) and credit solutions, including real estate-backed and structured financing. The AR 2025 describes a move to a relationship-centric advisory model for HNW and UHNW clients, with enhanced global custody and multi-asset execution. The MEED award page reports private banking clients up 18% year on year.

asset_management.detail: No in-house asset management subsidiary in Qatar. Doha Bank founded the QE Index ETF (QETF), which is managed by Aventicum Capital Management (Qatar). Its Indian associate, Doha Brokerage and Financial Services Ltd (35.29%), does brokerage and asset management in India. The Wealth Management Division reports AUM above USD 100m, but this reflects advisory and custody assets, not an asset manager.

brokerage.detail: Not through a Qatar subsidiary. QSE trading: Q-Trade in online and mobile banking links to the client's account at The Group Securities (accounts at other brokers cannot be linked). International: the Treasury & Investments 'International Brokerage' desk covers US, Canada, UK and Europe shares, ETFs and options from USD 5,000, with accounts opened at the Investments department. Margin trading is also offered.

digital_investing.detail: DB Global Markets (DBGM) platform on desktop and mobile: US and European stocks, bonds, FX, metals and commodities; account opening within one business day; 15% margin; revenue QAR 3.2m in 2025 (QAR 1.65m in 2024). Q-Trade gives QSE trading inside Doha Bank online and mobile banking via The Group Securities. The technology vendor for DBGM is not named.

advisory.detail: Private bankers give investment advice, using Bank of Singapore research and risk profiling. Financial planning and estate planning are also offered. The Euromoney 2026 award cites personalised advisory and financial planning.

discretionary.detail: No discretionary mandate offer found on the Private Banking pages, in the AR 2025 or in award coverage.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No robo-advisor or model-portfolio product found.

funds_platform.detail: Third-party mutual funds through the Bank of Singapore platform for Private Banking clients. The Euromoney 2026 'Best for Funds' (Qatar) award cites a diversified range of fund strategies. Shariah-compliant products were added in 2025.

structured_products.detail: Structured products through the Bank of Singapore platform; structured FX, commodity and rates hedging through Global Markets Solutions.

private_markets.detail: Strategic partnership with Blackstone, formed Q2 2025, giving Qatari institutional and HNW clients private equity, real estate, private credit, multi-asset credit and infrastructure strategies. MoU with Carlyle (30 Oct 2024) for evergreen private-markets solutions and an exclusive product for Qatar investors. MoU with KKR (22 Sep 2026) to explore access to KKR private equity, infrastructure, credit and real estate strategies. The Private Banking menu lists hedge funds, private-market funds and private equities. Won MEED 'Best Private Equity Offering - MENA' 2025.

islamic_wealth.detail: Conventional bank; Islamic banking was discontinued in 2011 under a QCB directive. In 2025 the Wealth Management Division introduced Shariah-compliant investment products to attract new clients.

initiatives.what: Signed an MoU with KKR at the Qatar Economic Forum (New York) to explore private-markets access for eligible Qatari investors.
Won Euromoney Private Banking Awards 2026 (Qatar) for Best Client Service and Best for Funds.
Board adopted a 5-year strategy (2026-2030) while the Himma Transformation (launched Oct 2023) continues. New board for 2026-2028; new Chief Private Banking & Wealth Management Officer listed.
Won MEED 'Best Private Equity Offering - MENA' (Wealth & Private Banking Awards 2025).

Wealth Management Division launched a Swiss global custody account with UBS and Shariah-compliant products and consolidated investment segments; AUM passed USD 100m. DBGM platform revenue nearly doubled to QAR 3.2m.
Strategic partnership formed with Blackstone (Q2 2025) for private capital strategies for Qatari investors.

opportunities: Doha Bank stacks alternatives partners (Blackstone 2025, Carlyle MoU 2024, KKR MoU Sep 2026) but distributes them through private bankers; no in-app or digital distribution of these products was found (S19, S18, S17, S8).
Wealth Management Division AUM is small (above USD 100m in 2025) and the division is described as recently started, so the proposition is still being built (S5).

No model portfolios, robo service or discretionary mandate found. Retail investing is limited to self-directed QSE trading through a third-party broker (Q-Trade) and the DBGM trading platform (S12, S13).
New wealth leadership (Chief Private Banking & Wealth Management Officer on the 2026 executive page) and a new 2026-2030 strategy (S1, S7).
barriers: Private Banking investment accounts already run on the Bank of Singapore platform, and custody is with UBS (S8, S5).
Large leadership turnover between the Governance Report 2025 and the Oct 2026 executive page (Deputy CEO, retail, treasury and HR heads no longer listed) makes the buyer map uncertain (S6, S1).
Customer deposits fell from QAR 57.7bn (Dec 2025) to QAR 55.5bn (Jun 2026), and legacy credit litigation is disclosed; balance-sheet focus may limit spend (S3, S6).
